test_title: PYST 19: SSC MTS - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 22 Oct 2021 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A and B working together can do 36% of a work in 9 days. B alone can do the work in 30 days. How long will A alone take to do the work?
solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A and B to do 36% of a work = 9 days

Time taken by B alone do the work = 30 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Time taken by A and B to do 36% of a work = 9

Time taken by A and B to do 100% of work = (9 × 100)/36

⇒ 900/36

⇒ 25 days

Time taken by B alone do the work = 30 days

LCM of 25 and 30 is 150

Efficiency of A and B = (150/25) = 6 

Efficiency of B = (150/30) = 5

Now,

Time taken by A alone to do the whole work = [150(6 – 5)] days

⇒ 150/1 days

⇒ 150 days

**∴ The required time taken by A alone is 150 days**
